text.p: Finnish forestry group Metsa-Serla Oy said on Thursday it expected a loss in the last four months of the year but would make a full-year profit.

"According to present estimates, Metsa-Serla's result after financial items for the last four months of the year is likely to show a loss," it said in a statement with its January-August results. "However, the result for the year is expected to show a profit," it said.
"Market pulp prices bottomed out during the spring, and a slight upward trend was visible by the end of the summer," it said. "Prices for fine papers are expected to embark on a modest rise."
Metsa-Serla said its fine paper mills' capacity utilisation rate was likely to be about 80 percent this year, but up at around 90 percent in the last four months.

"The improvement in product prices has not come in time to have any material effect on results for the final four months," it said, adding that an unspecified one-off cost of around 300 million markka would weigh on full-year earnings.
"The prospects for magazine paper prices for the rest of the year are unclear," it said.

In paperboard, improved demand was "a good opportunity to utilise the group's higher capacity", it said. Board mills were expected to have good order stocks, a decline in prices in foreign currencies seemed to have ceased and some prices had already strengthened.
"Demand for linerboard has improved during the summer and is expected to remain good for the rest of the year. Price rises are anticipated from October onwards," it said.
